blocks.text: 1. Data Cleaning
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446708808-313474021.png
Data Cleaning, covering how raw ingested content gets prepared for the rest of the pipeline, shifts focus from pulling data in to preparing it for use.
It removes noise from raw documents before they ever reach chunking.
2. Why Raw Content Is Noisy
Web crawling, PDF parsing, database ingestion, and API ingestion, all covered in Document Ingestion, each leave behind leftover artifacts from how the content was originally produced.
Navigation menus, repeated boilerplate, extraction glitches, and formatting noise all remain unless removed.

blocks.text: 3. Removing Boilerplate
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446709124-116394861.png
Web Crawling covered removing navigation menus and footers specifically.
The same boilerplate problem appears across every ingestion source, not just crawled pages.
4. Fixing Encoding Issues
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446709125-805649104.png
Text extracted from different sources arrives in different character encodings.
Mismatched encoding turns readable characters into garbled symbols unless normalized.

blocks.title: warn
blocks.content: A document with a mismatched encoding does not always fail loudly. It often produces readable looking but subtly wrong characters, like curly quotes turning into stray symbols, which degrades embedding quality without an obvious error.

blocks.text: 5. Handling Duplicate Whitespace
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446709126-692195938.png
Extracted text often carries repeated spaces, tabs, and blank lines.
Collapsing that whitespace keeps the cleaned document compact and readable.
6. Stripping Irrelevant Content
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446709126-80993822.png
Advertisements, cookie notices, and unrelated sidebars add no retrieval value.
Stripping that irrelevant content keeps embeddings focused on what actually matters.
7. Detecting Corrupted Extractions
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446709127-399368139.png
Some extractions fail silently, producing garbled or empty text.
This is a related detection challenge to OCR for scanned PDFs, covered generally in PDF Parsing.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: A simple safeguard flags any document whose cleaned text falls below a minimum length or character diversity threshold, catching corrupted extractions before they ever reach chunking.

blocks.text: 8. Cleaning As The Guard Step
Every document, regardless of its original ingestion source, passes through this same cleaning step.
It acts as one consistent guard before chunking, covered as a later module, ever begins.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Data Cleaning Needs Extra Attention

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Data Cleaning Needs Extra Attention
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446709127-404141317.png
Mixed source pipelines need consistent, thorough cleaning.
Already clean, curated internal text needs only light, minimal cleaning.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates collapsing whitespace and stripping irrelevant boilerplate.

code.content:
import re

raw_text = """
Home   |   About   |   Contact


   Welcome to our Documentation Page

This  section   explains   the API in detail.


Copyright 2026. All rights reserved.
"""

def clean_text(text):
    lines = text.split("\n")
    lines = [ln for ln in lines if "Copyright" not in ln and "|" not in ln]
    text = "\n".join(lines)

    text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\n\s*\n+", "\n\n", text)
    return text.strip()

cleaned = clean_text(raw_text)
print("Raw text:")
print(repr(raw_text))
print("\nCleaned text:")
print(repr(cleaned))

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows navigation boilerplate and a copyright footer removed, and repeated whitespace collapsed.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Skipping cleaning entirely because a source looks mostly readable at a glance.
Assuming every source shares the same character encoding without verifying it.
Leaving repeated whitespace and blank lines untouched, wasting space in later chunks.
Never checking for silently corrupted or empty extractions before they reach chunking.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Data cleaning removes noise from raw documents before they reach chunking.
Every raw source carries leftover artifacts from how it was originally produced.
Boilerplate removal applies across every ingestion source, not just crawled pages.
Mismatched encoding turns readable characters into garbled symbols unless normalized.
Collapsing duplicate whitespace keeps cleaned documents compact and readable.
Stripping irrelevant content like ads and sidebars keeps embeddings focused on what matters.
Corrupted or silently failed extractions should be detected before reaching chunking.
Cleaning acts as one consistent guard step regardless of the original ingestion source.
